description: The COLLATE clause's position among column constraints, through the SQL surface: the DESCRIBE TABLE type cell carries COLLATE '<spec>' and the constraint cells carry their marks. COLLATE moves freely around NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY and COMMENT, with one live-verified exception: it may not FOLLOW a DEFAULT - the default was already typed without the collation, so the refusal reads 'Default value data type does not match data type for column ...'. COLLATE before the DEFAULT is fine. Converted 1:1 from features/CollateConstraintOrderTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE test1 (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR COLLATE 'utf8' NOT NULL)
DESCRIBE TABLE test1
SELECT CONTAINS(UPPER(MAX(IFF("name" = 'NAME', "type", NULL))), 'COLLATE ''UTF8'''), MAX(IFF("name" = 'NAME', "null?", NULL)) FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
